title: 河洛群俠傳 (Ho Tu Lo Shu ： The Books of Dragon)
notes: Started from Highball's library (`steam.exe -silent -applaunch 952860`), played about 9 minutes (12:57:46 to 13:07:21, the last frame the log recorded): the opening village and the terrain around it. The captures are 3838x2160, 3838x2160 and 3840x2158 — the panel's full 3840x2160, i.e. 2x of a 1920x1080 desktop. This launch log carries no `Setting display mode:` line, unlike the other games I ran today, so the game did not switch the display itself: it ran full screen on the HiDPI desktop. Frame rate on the Metal HUD (bottom left): 22.69 fps in the village at the game's own 1920x1080, 22.20 fps with the 视讯 settings page open, and 29.85 fps in the same village after the resolution was dropped to 1600x900. The resolution is the lever here — 1600x900 is about 30% fewer pixels and gave about 30% more frames, which is the shape of a title that is GPU-bound rather than CPU- or sync-bound at that size. It never stuttered and never hitched; it is just short of smooth, which is the whole of the rating. The game's own 视讯 page, for context: 分辨率 1920x1080, 画面模式 全屏, 画面质量 自定义, 物件可见距离 1.17, 阴影距离 96, 垂直同步 off, 反锯齿 低, 植被品质 中, 粒子密度 0.50, 体积光分辨率 / 环境光质量 / 云层品质 all 低, 环境光遮蔽 and 动态模糊 off, 阴影增强 / 高光 / 光线适应 on. Its `System.setting` in the game folder agrees on the numbers (ShadowDistance 96, VSync false, AntiAliasing 1, Vegetation Package 1 with VisibleDistance 60, CullingDistanceMultiplier 1.17246377) and is dated 13:02, the moment the last apply landed. The applied resolution is visible in the bottle's registry: `[Software\Heluo\J2]` `Screenmanager Resolution Width/Height` now read 1600x900, where the same keys read 1920x1080 for 古龙风云录, the other Heluo title I ran an hour earlier. Unity 2019.3.14f1 (Mono), 64-bit, D3D11 (feature level 11_1). DXMT loaded and did not fall back to wined3d. No mods: there is no `steamapps/workshop/content/952860`, even though the store page does list Steam Workshop for this title. Nothing to report beyond the frame rate — no crash, and no crash handler output. Its own `Player.log` is the noisiest of the six games, but all of the noise is in the game's own managed code: 3,810 of 3,813 `NullReferenceException`s come out of its animation footstep-sound node (`Heluo.Animation.MoveSoundEventNode.Execute` → `AnimatorEventTrack.Update` → `AnimatorEventPlayer.OnStateUpdate`), 3 out of `GPUInstancer.GPUInstancerDetailManager+<FillCellsDetailDataCoroutine>`, plus 2 `ERROR: Shader Hidden/Nature/Terrain/Utilities shader is not supported on this GPU`. There is no Wine or DXMT frame anywhere in those traces, the footstep sounds still resolve and play (461 `Audio Path : Resources_Audio/SoundEffect/Footsteps_Sound/…` lines), and the same signature is in the previous session's log from 10-07 (2,177 of them). None of it showed on screen. For the page: the store name already carries the English title — `河洛群俠傳 (Ho Tu Lo Shu ： The Books of Dragon)` — so the slug needs no romanisation beyond dropping the Chinese half. (Heluo / 香港商河洛互動娛樂股份有限公司, published with 方块游戏, 14 Nov 2018. Note the interface and subtitles are Chinese only; English is not supported.)
issues: Frame rate: 22.69 fps walking the village at 1920x1080, 29.85 fps in the same area after dropping the resolution to 1600x900. Playable and steady, but the lowest of the six games I ran today.
